title: Patch the signal
description: Connect two generated sources through a filter or directly to an output, then audition the resulting route.
useCase: Make audio routing topology editable and show which connections actually reach the output.
interaction: Drag an output socket to an input, or select both with keyboard or touch. Listen opts into audio; connection chips remove cables.
reducedMotion: New-cable fades are removed for keyboard input and reduced motion. Audio remains explicit opt-in; host pause, tab hiding and unmount stop and close the owned audio context.
limitations: Two quiet generated oscillators, one fixed low-pass filter, one output and at most three cables. No microphone, samples, node creation or arbitrary graphs. The output meter reads an AnalyserNode; audio quality is not a physical-device certification.
look: Graphite studio panel with steel socket rings, ivory and red cables, restrained module labels and a small measured output level.
motion: A tentative cable follows the pointer; a valid drop creates a curved route with a 160 ms fade. The output level follows real generated audio only after Listen.
adapt: `connect` enforces the bounded routing rules and `cables` is the topology. `listen` creates native audio nodes; `stop` disposes them. `DEFAULT_CONFIG` and the `config` prop expose source spacing, audition pitch, incompatible ports and cable timing.
